title: Did They Get the Right Guys?

lines.text: Hiya. I'd like you to meet my car.
It's not much to look at. Rubbish old thing, really.
But it's my faithful runaround, and I love it.
Last week, somebody stole it.
And by the end of the week, I wasn't sure who.
Hang on.
No. No, no, no.
Hello, police? I'd like to report a stolen car.
Right you are. I'll give you a crime number.
A crime number. That's that, then. Could be weeks.
Good news, sir. We've found your vehicle.
Already? Brilliant! Where is it?
About two miles down the road from you.
Oh, great. I'll walk down there.
Oh, no, you can't have it. We need to impound it for the investigation.
Is there much damage?
A broken window. And the steering column shroud's missing.
Honestly, I'm not fussed about catching anyone. It's a rubbish old car.
If it drives, I'll just walk down and drive it home.
Sorry, sir. It has to come in.
Hear that? The gears of the system, engaging.
Okie-dokie. Let me know when I can come and get it.
Yep, you can come and get your car.
Brilliant. Where are you?
The impound lot. It's about fifteen miles out.
Right. And you close at...?
Five. And we're not open at the weekend.
Half an hour. Fifteen miles. No car. No bus.
Right. Okay. Monday, then.
Saturday. I know exactly where my car is.
Sitting in a secure compound, having a quiet weekend off.
Which is more than I'm getting.
Yeah, sorry. I need to take the day off. It's an emergency.
Oh no. What's happened?
I'm collecting my own car.
There it is. Reunited at last.
That's four nights at a hundred and twenty-five pounds a night. Five hundred pounds, please.
Hang on a minute. Four nights?
I couldn't pick it up on Friday, because you were closing.
Yeah. We charge you for the Saturday and Sunday.
I offered to collect it on Thursday, and you wouldn't let me!
You're charging me rent, for the days you kept my car against my will.
Well, yeah. Sorry. That's how it works.
It's like a little gravitational anomaly. It only consumes cash.
So, I wrote the police a formal complaint. My agent helped me keep it polite.
And I asked one simple question.
What's the legal term, when someone takes your property without permission,
and refuses to give it back unless you pay them?
Because I always thought that was called extortion.
Now. Let's be fair to the thieves. They broke one window.
Took my car for a thirty-minute spin, and left it two miles down the road.
I could have swept up the glass and been driving it by Thursday teatime.
The service my taxes pay for kept my car for a long weekend,
cost me a day off work, and five hundred quid.
And covered it in this silver fingerprint powder. Which does not come off.
So you tell me.
Did they get the right guys?
